Source of data UNICRI administered a survey to collect information from national authority in the Eastern Partnership Countries.Kindly find below the feedback received from Armenia and Moldova.ArmeniaSPMC Financial Intelligence Unit the Golden Palace hotel was sold in auction in 2022 USD 10.5 million after it was donated to the State following accusation of a former chief of the Armenian customs service. The buyer has the responsibility to invest an additional USD one million in the next five years to improve the quality of the hotel for the benefit of the touristic region where it is located as well as more broadly for the benefit of Armenia and its people. As a result of the investment plan the hotel complex is expected to generate 100 new jobs and to foster economic development. Between March and May 2020 the hotel served as a COVID19 isolation center. From OctoberNovember 2021 for around one year the hotel hosted more than 30 displaced families from the Nagorno Karabakh region. The decision was taken by the Government of Armenia in cooperation with NGOs who also contributed with donationsfunding e.g. 3 mealsday400 people.MoldovaCARA Within the framework of the Luca Filat case in 2021 the UK and Moldova signed a MoU whereby the UK returned around GBP 458 000 to Moldova. The agreement foresees that funds returned must be used for social assistance benefitting vulnerable people in Moldova people with severe disabilities. According to the plan the local authorities will hire 566 personal assistants for four months. In this context Moldova appointed a CSO to monitor and evaluate the transparent expenditure of the returned funds.

comment.narrative: No feedback is available prior to project initiation
Positive feedback is collected from national counterparts with respect to value of project interventions

National counterparts regularly conveyed positive and constructive feedback with respect to the value of project interventions.For instance as a followup to the Expert Study Mission to Brussels and to The Hague UNICRI developed a short survey asking the participants for feedback to better understand their needs and requests both in view of future missions and within the wider scope of the cooperation framework of the EU funded project Support to EU Eastern Partnership Countries to Enhance Asset Recovery. Feedback received from officials in the EaP countries following the Expert Study Mission to Brussels was overall very positive. For example representatives from the PGO of Georgia said assistance provided by UNICRI is significant and greatly appreciated. We would welcome the continuation of our mutual cooperation. Colleagues from NABU Ukraine similarly conveyed that based on conversations with colleagues from foreign jurisdictions and their practices we understand that Ukraine needs to extend the use of civil confiscation and UNICRI continued assistance in this regard would be critical.The overall feedback received after the Study Mission to The Hague was also very good and among some of the main needs and requests identified were the desire to continue sharing best practices at the international level together with the need for more case studies and for other study missions of this kind. For example officials from Georgias PGO stated that their expectation prior to the mission was to upgrade knowledge regarding the asset management system of the Netherlands expectation that was fully met with the desire that UNICRI could support us in the development of good mechanisms for asset recovery and for the fight against organised crime corruption and illicit financial flows by continuing to provide access to best international practices in these areas.
